causes.source_quote: Organic heart damage (coronary artery disease, mitral stenosis or incompetence, inflammatory and degenerative changes in the heart muscle, hyperthyroidism or toxic effects of alcohol excess). In some cases no cause is found (i.e. lone AF) It may be seen in normal subjects, particularly during emotional stress or following surgery, exercise, or acute alcoholic intoxication.

summary.source_quote: Atrial fibrillation (AF) is characterised by disorganised atrial activity. When an abnormally high atrial rate develops, irregular transmission of stimuli to the ventricles occurs resulting in a rapid, irregular heart rate. AF is a common cardiac rhythm disturbance. It may occur as a brief symptom- free episode with transient bouts of irregular heart beat or as a sustained form of arrhythmia (paroxysmal AF or transient AF). Episodes of AF may spontaneously revert to normal sinus rhythm or may enter a chronic stage. Although AF may present as a transient episode in otherwise fit subjects it usually is an indication of associated cardiac disease.
